verdict.rationale: Svelte's first-party docs describe declarative components whose script runs per component instance, with $state providing reactive local state and component-scoped CSS for encapsulation. Community reports corroborate building large, complex UIs from Svelte components, using Context to share state between them. Missing for 10: first-party documentation in the pack of explicit composition mechanics (props, child components, slots/snippets) for nesting components.

support.subject: As a developer, I can build encapsulated components that manage their own local state and compose them into complex UIs

citations.quote: A `<script>` block contains JavaScript (or TypeScript, when adding the `lang="ts"` attribute) that runs when a component instance is created.
The `$state` rune allows you to create _reactive state_, which means that your UI _reacts_ when it changes.
CSS inside a `<style>` block will be scoped to that component.
Svelte Stores and the Context system are great for sharing state
Their team migrated a huge, complex React app to Svelte/SvelteKit in a month
